reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?
Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Not a single sample compares 1/2 with 1/4. Seeds 42, 43 and 46 ask 'A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?', which is fraction identification and duplicates the neighbouring illustrate competency, while seeds 44 and 45 render whole-number items, 'Compare the numbers: 10 ___ 6' and 'Compare the numbers: 18 ___ 30'. The word 'compare' is honoured only by comparing integers, never fractions.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Neither direction of the intended comparison is ever generated: no item keys that 1/2 is greater than 1/4, none keys that 1/4 is less than 1/2, and none establishes the essential precondition that the two wholes must be the same size. The phrase 'using models' names a required representation, and no shaded-strip or partitioned-circle comparison of the two fractions is produced anywhere in seeds 42 to 46.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The fraction stems are pitched fine for Quarter 4, but the injected integer items are not: seed 45 compares 18 with 30, a two-digit magnitude comparison that has nothing to do with fractional parts and that a child working on halves and fourths will find contextually bewildering, and the 'cannot be determined' option in both integer items is abstract test-taking language rather than a plausible Grade 1 misconception.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The node contains just two stem shapes, one repeated fraction-naming template drawn three times and one repeated integer-comparison template drawn twice. The variations a comparison competency needs, comparing shaded area in two pictures, comparing shares of the same cake between two and four children, and ordering the unit fractions, are wholly absent.

competency_alignment.rationale: The apparent difficulty progression runs from naming 1/2 at seeds 42 and 43 to comparing 10 with 6 and then 18 with 30 at seeds 44 and 45, meaning difficulty is escalated by enlarging whole numbers. That builds symbolic integer comparison, a Quarter 1 number-sense skill, and moves directly away from comparing fractional parts of a whole using models.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency's entire numeric world is the denominators 2 and 4 and the single whole they partition, yet seed 45 places 30 in a stem and seed 44 places 10 and 6. Those magnitudes exceed anything this fraction competency licenses and confirm that a foreign number-comparison generator is supplying items to a fractions node.
